newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Computer bug eats into MUSIC Q1 revenue.
newsitem.headline: Computer bug eats into MUSIC Q1 revenue.

text.p: A computer bug delayed launch of a new software product of Music Semiconductors Corp and was responsible for the firm missing its first quarter revenue target of 107.7 million pesos, president Michael Burton said.
Earlier on Wednesday, the company announced a net revenue of 104.7 million pesos during the period.

Burton said the voice processing board software, which will enable computer terminals to perform facsimile and other value-added telephone functions, was supposed to be launched in the first quarter but test marketing revealed it had some problems with applications.
The company was expecting $2 million sales from the new product for 1997.
The company designs, manufactures and markets specialised computer network technologies for large computer companies overseas.
Burton remained confident the company would be able to solve the problem, although he declined to give a timetable for the launch of the product.
"We are still working those bugs out. We're working very hard on to fix the problem," Burton told analysts.
Burton also expressed concern that the introduction of new products could encounter some delays due to the dearth of competent engineers to develop the products.
"It's a continuing struggle to find qualified people," he said, adding that specialised engineers are like star athletes who demand high compensation packages and are prone to pirating.
"It has hurt and we would expect that it will continue to hurt our product introduction timing," he added.
Despite the delays, the company was able to slightly exceed its net income target. It posted 19.4 million peso net income in the first three months of the year, Burton said.
He said the company was maintaining its full-year revenue target of 817.6 million pesos and a net income level of 249 million pesos.
He attributed the first quarter income growth to higher sales of its traditional computer networking chips.
"The medium and long term picture in sales continue to look pretty good," he said. Conversion $1 = 26.3 pesos
